reason: Source inspection (kernel.py lines 17-19) shows take = v >= best in a forward scan, so a later expert with a logit equal to the current best replaces it — the HIGHEST tied index wins, not the lowest. Runtime probe t6 confirmed this on real CUDA inputs: rows [3,3,3,1], [1,3,3,0], [2,1,0.5,2] have tied maxima {0,1,2}, {1,2}, {0,3}, and route_top1 returned [2,2,3] instead of the contract-mandated [0,1,0]. problem.txt explicitly requires the LOWEST tied index to win and declares ties a normal occurrence, so the failure is in-scope (claim c2, confirmed, in_scope, evidence c2.e1). Verdict: reject.
